page_01: Penguins slide across the ice on their bellies. It's called tobogganing!
page_02: Under its white-looking fur, a polar bear has black skin!
page_03: Arctic foxes wrap their fluffy tails around themselves like a warm blanket.
page_04: Snowy owls often hunt in the daytime, unlike most owls!
page_05: A reindeer's nose warms up icy air before it reaches its lungs.
page_06: Baby harp seals are born with fluffy white fur to keep them warm.
page_07: Walruses use their long tusks to pull themselves out of the water!
page_08: Emperor penguins huddle together and take turns in the warm middle.
page_09: A narwhal's long tusk is actually a tooth!
page_10: Beluga whales chirp and whistle so much they're called sea canaries!
page_11: Moose are great swimmers and can dive underwater to eat plants!
page_12: Arctic hares can hop on just their back legs, like kangaroos!
page_13: Snowshoe hares turn white in winter and brown in summer.
page_14: Huskies sleep with their fluffy tails over their noses to stay warm.
page_15: A puffin can flap its wings up to 400 times a minute!
page_16: Bears can sleep through most of the winter without eating!
page_17: Chipmunks fill their burrows with snacks to eat all winter long.
page_18: Cardinals stay bright and colorful all winter long!
page_19: Chickadees hide seeds in hundreds of places and remember where!
page_20: Snow leopards wrap their long, fluffy tails around them like a scarf.
page_21: Red pandas have an extra wrist bone that works like a thumb!
page_22: Mountain goats have grippy hooves that work like hiking boots!
page_23: Bison sweep snow aside with their big heads to find grass.
page_24: Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal in the world!
page_25: Ermines turn white in winter, except for the dark tip of their tail.
page_26: Musk oxen grow a super-soft, super-warm wool called qiviut.
page_27: A lynx has big furry paws that work like snowshoes!
page_28: Raccoons nap a lot in winter, but they don't truly hibernate.
page_29: Deer grow a thicker, fluffier coat to stay cozy in winter.
page_30: Foxes can hear a mouse moving under the snow, then pounce!
page_31: Snowflakes form high up in the clouds, one tiny ice crystal at a time.
page_33: Penguins can't fly in the sky, but they fly underwater!
page_34: Polar bears can swim for days without resting!
page_35: People in Mexico were sipping cocoa drinks thousands of years ago!
page_36: Inside an igloo, it can be much warmer than outside!
page_37: Arctic foxes have fur on the bottoms of their paws!
page_38: Sea otters hold paws while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
page_39: The biggest snowball fight ever had more than 7,600 people!
page_40: Snow is really clear ice. It looks white because it bounces light!
page_41: Both boy and girl reindeer grow antlers!
page_42: Emperor penguin dads keep their egg warm on their feet all winter!
page_43: A polar bear can smell food from far, far away!
page_44: The biggest gingerbread house ever was big enough to walk inside!
page_45: An owl can turn its head almost all the way around!
page_46: Gingerbread cookies have been baked for more than 400 years!
page_47: Moose can turn their big ears to hear sounds from far away.
page_48: Huskies love to run and can pull a sled for miles and miles!
page_49: Harp seals can hold their breath underwater for about 15 minutes!
page_50: Happy winter from the Snowy Cuties!
